name: Medtronic
description: Medtronic makes implantable and surgical medical devices and sells them to hospitals and healthcare systems in more than 150 countries. Its three reportable segments are Cardiovascular (pacemakers, defibrillators, heart valves, stents, catheters including cardiac ablation), Neuroscience (spinal implants and robotics, brain and nerve stimulators, neurovascular) and Medical Surgical (surgical tools, energy devices, endoscopy, patient monitoring), plus a Diabetes business (insulin pumps and glucose sensors) being separated as MiniMed. Revenue is mostly device sales tied to procedures, with consumables, leads and sensors recurring after the implant.

sub.name: Surgical and hospital devices and diagnostics

employees.note: "over 95,000 full-time employees", 43 percent based in the US.

businessLines.name: Cardiovascular
businessLines.how: Sells implantable devices and procedure-specific disposables (pacemakers, defibrillators, cardiac ablation catheters, transcatheter heart valves, stents) to hospitals, one-time per procedure, with replacement cycles and recurring consumables.

operatingProfit.period: FY2026 (year ended 2026-04-24), reportable segment operating profit (excludes amortisation of intangibles, restructuring and other items)

businessLines.name: Neuroscience
businessLines.how: Sells spinal implants with robotics and navigation (capital plus per-procedure implants), neuromodulation devices (deep brain and spinal cord stimulators, sacral and tibial) and neurovascular products to hospitals; implant revenue plus follow-on consumables and replacement devices.

operatingProfit.period: FY2026 (year ended 2026-04-24), reportable segment operating profit (excludes amortisation of intangibles, restructuring and other items)

businessLines.name: Medical Surgical
businessLines.how: Sells surgical staplers, energy devices (LigaSure), endoscopy and hernia products, plus patient monitoring and respiratory equipment, to hospitals; mostly disposables per procedure plus some capital equipment.

operatingProfit.period: FY2026 (year ended 2026-04-24), reportable segment operating profit (excludes amortisation of intangibles, restructuring and other items)

businessLines.name: Diabetes (MiniMed, being separated)
businessLines.how: Sells insulin pumps and continuous glucose monitors to patients, paid by insurers and health systems; the pump is a one-time sale while sensors, infusion sets and other consumables recur.

brands.name: Hugo robotic-assisted surgery system
brands.note: Soft-tissue robotic surgery; no revenue disclosed

brands.name: MiniMed Group, Inc. (Diabetes business)
brands.note: IPO completed 2026-03-09 on Nasdaq selling about 10 percent; Medtronic retains about 90.03 percent (252,813,348 shares) and still consolidates it; plans to complete separation within the next fiscal year. FY2026 net sales $3,112M.

whatsNext.text: Complete the separation of the Diabetes business (MiniMed) within the next fiscal year; further steps or sale of the remaining ownership subject to market conditions

Blackstone development-funding agreements: Blackstone eligible for milestone payments up to $1.2 billion and royalties after US approval and launch of funded products; one Diabetes product was FDA-approved in Q4 FY2026
